cohort: 602 adolescent mothers (10-19 years old) and 602 adult mothers (20-29 years old) in a tertiary care hospital in Tamil Nadu, India.
finding: Adolescent pregnancies were associated with increased risk of adverse maternal (anemia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, premature rupture of membranes) and neonatal outcomes (preterm birth, low birth weight, birth asphyxia, intrauterine and neonatal death, and neonatal hospitalizations).
birth_weight: Low birth weight was more common among neonates born to adolescent mothers.
